browserInspection.harness: npm run rehearse (scripts/rehearse): headless Chromium (playwright-core), the production build of this commit, a simulated native host answering the Tauri commands from a data directory, real key presses through main.ts. The library is first left alone until its background work ends, with the progress line checked throughout. Pass or fail by invariants; timings are reports.

invariants.invariant: a line shows only under the score being prepared
the line is gone once the work ends
a pitch choice names the edition the library installed
no pitch choice is left on an edition installed on the way
a second visit to the library engraves no edition again
the edition shown was drawn by the current engraver
a layout switch that keeps the edition writes only the choice of layout
Fingers draws at its last measure
an early press runs exactly once
the simulated host answered every command

firstOpenAfterIdle.note: Janko layout (the owner's), a fresh writable copy of the private data copy for each run, each score opened in library order with Back in between. "At once": opened as soon as the library showed. "After idle": the library was left alone until no score was being prepared and no line showed for 6 s (45 s; 5 scores worked on, 5 with a line), so its background work (viewer PRs 214, 216, 217, 222) had run. The simulated host starts with an empty derived-file store. Measured on a shared, loaded build host.

browserInspection.limits: Headless Chromium with a simulated native host, not WebView2 or WKWebView, not an installed package. Physical MIDI, audio, practice at a keyboard and the pianist's musical acceptance were not observed. A key pressed while the opening dialog still shows its progress can be ignored by design; none is lost once the score is drawn.
